_comment: skfem helmholtz#6: complex Helmholtz output must be split into .real and np.abs. Verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / meshio 5.3.5: the pathology is real but the claim's quoted texts are wrong. meshio never says 'Cannot write complex array' -- .vtu raises KeyError: dtype('complex128'), .xdmf raises KeyError: 'complex128', and skfem's own Mesh.save propagates the same KeyError; nothing is truncated silently because no file is produced. The genuinely silent half is ndarray.tofile: it writes 2x the bytes and a float64 reader gets a doubled array with real and imaginary parts INTERLEAVED (not the real part). Writing {'u_real': u.real, 'u_abs': np.abs(u)} round-trips both fields. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 sets WRITE_PAYLOAD to 'abs', so the payload handed to ndarray.tofile and to the meshio / Mesh.save writers is the real-valued np.abs(u) half of the documented .real / np.abs split instead of the raw complex vector. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 18 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 10 of them, among them 'payload_dtype=complex128', 'tofile_bytes_is_double=True', 'float64_readback_is_interleaved=True', 'vtu_writer_error_type=KeyError' and "dtype('complex128')", so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
